headlines.summary: Follow below as CNBC highlights the biggest stock moves of the day.
headlines.article_text: Stocks moving the most today: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Samuel Boivin | Nurphoto | Getty Images A slate of artificial intelligence stocks surged on the heels of Jensen Huang's return to the helm of Nvidia, with CoreWeave and Micron Technology soaring on Monday. A rally in gold prices also lifted shares of mining stocks like Newmont and Gold Fields. Follow below as CNBC highlights the biggest stock moves of the day. 11 Min Ago Symbiotic slumps after revenue forecast largely disappoints The automation technology company slipped in extended trading. Guidance for first quarter revenue ranges from $805 million to $825 million, while the FactSet consensus sought $822 million. Symbiotic shares were last off almost 4%. Symbiotic on Monday In the fourth quarter, adjusted EBITDA of $113.9 million and revenue of $777.6 million beat analysts' respective estimates of $103.9 million and $774.2 million, per LSEG. — Darla Mercado 7 Min Ago Semtech shares drop despite the company beating estimates Shares of Semtech were down 8.5% despite the semiconductors provider beating analyst consensus on earnings per share and revenue. SMTC on Monday Semtech reported $1.17 in earnings per share, excluding items, and $423 million in revenue for the third quarter. Analysts polled by FactSet expected $1.13 earnings per share and $416.7 million in revenue. For the fourth quarter, the company expects earnings per share of $1.30 to $1.36, excluding items, and revenue of $475 million to $485 million. Both are above FactSet consensus estimates of $1.29 per share and $449.3 million. — Ananya Chetia 22 Min Ago Peloton Interactive jumps on $300 million share buyback announcement The fitness tech company saw shares pop 3% in extended trading after announcing that its board has authorized a $300 million share repurchase program. Peloton on Monday This program doesn't obligate Peloton to buy a specific amount of shares. — Darla Mercado 29 Min Ago Agilent Technologies rises in after-hours trading after guidance surpasses estimates Shares of Agilent Technologies jumped 7% after the company shared an outlook that topped the Street's expectations. Current-quarter guidance calls for adjusted earnings of $1.54 to $1.57 per share on revenue of $8 billion to $8.15 billion. The FactSet consensus estimate was $1.50 per share and $1.92 billion. Agilent's full-year forecast also came in ahead of analysts' expectations. — Darla Mercado 4 Hours Ago Mining stocks rally alongside the price of gold and copper December gold futures rallied Monday Mining stocks rallied Monday alongside bullish moves in the price of gold, silver and copper. Gold futures climbed about 4%, silver by roughly 5% and copper added nearly 3%. Newmont Mining , AngloGold Ashanti , Coeur Mining and Gold Fields Ltd. all surged more than 7%, while Freeport McMoRan jumped almost 8%. — Scott Schnipper 4 Hours Ago IP shares fall after its board approves spinoff In this photo illustration, the International Paper logo seen on a smartphone and on a computer screen. Pavlo Gonchar | SOPA Images | Lightrocket | Getty Images Shares of International Paper fell 4% after the packaging solutions company announced Monday that its board had approved the spinoff of its Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA) packaging business into a publicly traded company, DS Smith. International Paper will remain an important shareholder, retaining a 19.9% stake. The company expects to complete the separation and distribution on Dec. 7, 2026, after the satisfaction of customary conditions and regulatory approvals are met. Additionally, the company announced its intention to delist from the London Stock Exchange after the completion of the separation. — Deena Zaidi 4 Hours Ago Artificial intelligence names are soaring as Huang returns to Nvidia A slate of stocks linked to the artificial intelligence trade skyrocketed on Monday as Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO. Dell Technologies and neocloud CoreWeave were last up about 22%, while data center power play Bloom Energy surged 19%. Photonics stock Lumentum popped 18%. Memory stocks also surged, with the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) gaining 19%. Rallies in SK Hynix and Micron Technology , both up around 20%, lifted the ETF. — Darla Mercado 4 Hours Ago Boeing shares rise after President Trump says he expects China to buy 250 more aircraft President of China Xi Jinping (L) shakes hands with U.S. President Donald Trump during an arrival ceremony at the White House on September 24, 2026 in Washington, DC. Chip Somodevilla | Getty Images News | Getty Images Shares of Boeing popped over 4% after President Donald Trump said on CNBC's " Squawk on the Street " that he expects China to buy another 250 Boeing jets. BA News of the additional aircraft orders comes roughly six months after the May summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Trump. At the time, Trump said that China would purchase 200 Boeing jets , an agreement that Beijing confirmed . — Ananya Chetia 7 Hours Ago CoreWeave, Oracle surge on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang return Visual China Group | Getty Images Shares of CoreWeave and Oracle jumped 20% and 12%, respectively, following the announcement that Jensen Huang was returning as Nvidia CEO. The companies, as well as neoclouds like Nebius and IREN , were among the hardest hit after Huang's resignation ignited fears about Nvidia's role in financing AI companies . The company, known as the "central bank of AI," had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July. Oracle lost 10% in the last month, while CoreWeave sank 13%. Nebius and IREN lost 37% and nearly 40%, respectively, during that time. Nebius rose 29% and IREN gained 27% on Monday. — Michelle Fox 8 Hours Ago Nvidia surges after reinstating Huang as CEO Shares of Nvidia surged 28% in premarket trading after the company reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO . Huang stepped down Nov. 12 amid an adultery scandal, sending the stock plummeting and igniting fears over the artificial intelligence trade. Nvidia is down 40.5% in the past month. — Michelle Fox 9 Hours Ago General Motors moves higher after report on Barra successor CEO and Chair of General Motors Mary Barra delivers a speech during the brand's annual technology event in New York on Oct. 21, 2026. Charly Triballeau | AFP | Getty Images Shares of General Motors added more than 2% following a Bloomberg report that said executive Sterling Anderson is being considered as a potential successor to CEO Mary Barra. The company's board wants the next leader to have an expertise in software and self-driving technology, Bloomberg said, citing people familiar with the board's thinking. Anderson came to GM in June 2025, leaving behind the self-driving vehicle technology startup he co-founded, Aurora Innovation. Prior to that he was the director of autopilot programs at Tesla. — Michelle Fox 9 Hours Ago Dollar General rises on upgrade A Dollar General store in Denver, Colorado, US, on Wednesday, Aug. 26, 2026. Chet Strange | Bloomberg | Getty Images Shares of Dollar General moved 2% higher on the back of an upgrade to overweight from neutral at Piper Sandler. Analyst Peter Keith said comparable sales growth and margin expansion should help the discount retailer reach a high-teens earnings-per-share compound annual growth rate over the next three years. Plus, the company's steady growth profile is appealing in an increasingly volatile market environment, he said. — Michelle Fox 10 Hours Ago LuxExperience pops after JPMorgan upgrade JPMorgan upgraded the luxury digital retailer to overweight from neutral on Monday, sending U.S.-listed shares up 6.6% in premarket trading. headlines.article_text: Tech stocks see monster rally after Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Tech stock fortunes turned around following a torrid week for sector names that culminated in a steep sell-off Friday. Most major tech and AI buildout stocks rebounded. Nvidia bounced back sharply after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO. In this article NVDA CRWV NBIS GOOGL META MU Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 5:00 05:00 'Squawk on the Street’ crew react to Nvidia reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO Squawk on the Street Major tech stocks rebounded across the board Monday, sharply reversing Friday's steep sell-off when artificial intelligence stocks fell in the Nasdaq's worst week since 2020. Shares of Nvidia surged 31.48% after the company announced Monday morning that Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO . The semiconductor giant gained back nearly $1 trillion in market cap, posting its best day since May 2003. Nvidia's surge and Huang's reinstatement followed a more than 40% slump in the stock over the past month. The company has been embattled as reports surfaced about Huang's multiple extramarital affairs — one of which was with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes to be a Chinese spy. Huang resigned as CEO of the company he founded on Nov. 12. The Nasdaq Composite surged 6.51% Monday, for its best day since April 9, 2025. The Nasdaq slid 10% last week, with tech stocks having a rocky week as investors remained nervous about the valuation of some AI companies and business models. All three major averages ended last week in correction territory, and the Nasdaq turned negative for 2026. Nvidia stock chart Shares of Big Tech companies and other stocks related to the AI trade saw a lift Monday on the Nvidia news. Shares of Alphabet surged 6.34%, Meta gained 6.55%, Amazon jumped 3.47% and Microsoft increased 1.65%. SpaceX added 4.35%, Arm Holdings surged 16.08% and AMD added 6.85%. Dell and Micron posted some of the sector's biggest gains of the day, gaining 20.46% and 19.04%, respectively. The iShares Semiconductor ETF gained 13.63%. Neoclouds, which have seen a particularly choppy few months amid AI boom financing concerns, surged on Huang's reinstatement. Nebius soared 20.28%, CoreWeave gained 22.32% and Iren gained 23.86%. Following a brief premarket surge, Anthropic shares posted a decline of 1.43% in its third day of trading. Anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO. The stock gained 17% in its debut on Thursday, before closing down 8.5% on Friday. Read more CNBC tech news Nvidia skyrockets 30% on Huang’s return as CEO, recovering nearly all the losses since he disclosed affair U.S. probes Megaspeed, Alice Huang as new figure emerges in Nvidia chip case Anthropic's record IPO collides with tech's worst week on Wall Street since 2020 CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler in $44 billion deal as AI supercharges cyberattacks SpaceX sued by Oregon and Virginia over AI deepfake porn, Grok safety claims Speaking to CNBC's Eamon Javers about Huang's reinstatement, President Donald Trump on Monday said that last week's market sell-off "probably" influenced his support for the ousted CEO's return. "Probably so, but the bigger impact was the long term. The bigger impact was, he's got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about," Trump said on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." Trump said he spoke to Nvidia's board directly and that he "convinced" the board to reinstate Huang, who the president said "did nothing wrong." headlines.article_text: CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler in $44B deal as AI supercharges cyberattacks Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points CrowdStrike agreed to acquire network security provider Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at $43.9 billion. The deal is expected to close during the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal year 2028. Cybersecurity vendors have been on an acquisition spree to keep pace with AI-powered threats. In this article CRWD ZS Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 4:05 04:05 Dan Ives: This is just the start of a golden age for cybersecurity Morning Call CrowdStrike plans to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in an all-stock deal that combines two significant security businesses at a time when artificial intelligence is supercharging attacks. Shares of CrowdStrike dropped 9% on Monday, while Zscaler surged nearly 18%. The deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal year 2028. Under the agreement, Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each share. CrowdStrike's acquisition pushes the Austin, Texas-based cyber vendor into the network security market and comes amid a massive year for cybersecurity deal-making in the wake of high-profile hacks like Hugging Face. "With Zscaler, we're building cybersecurity's operating system: a single control plane to deploy AI, control AI, and enable any agentic application to run safely," CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said in a statement. "We see a path to become the largest AI safety and security company the world has ever seen." Recent outages affecting Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration and JPMorgan Chase have sparked anxiety as businesses accelerate software patching and upgrades to aging systems in an effort to prevent bad actors from exploiting software vulnerabilities with AI. CrowdStrike has been a major beneficiary of skyrocketing demand for AI security, with shares soaring about 80% this year as of Monday's open. Zscaler shares are up about 5% year to date after Monday's surge. Their combined market value exceeded $265 billion as of Friday's close, behind market leader Palo Alto Networks at $282 billion. The deal marks CrowdStrike's biggest acquisition to date and is among the largest in the sector as businesses consolidate and ramp up defenses to fend off AI-powered attacks. Last year, Google announced plans to acquire Wiz for $32 billion. In 2024 Cisco shelled about $28 billion for Splunk. Competitor Palo Alto Networks has also spent billions on several cyber and AI businesses, including startup Applied Compute and a $25 billion deal for CyberArk, which it closed earlier this year. Analysts view the Zscaler deal as a major AI security opportunity, allowing CrowdStrike to capture more customer security spending and close a significant gap with Palo Alto. "The addition of ZS to CRWD's platform could bring more breadth in an era of vendor consolidation and, more importantly, network security to position the company more effectively for rising demand for AI Sovereignty," wrote analysts at JPMorgan. CrowdStrike on Monday also reported better-than-expected fiscal third-quarter results , including earnings of 34 cents per share on $1.58 billion in revenue. That topped the 31 cents per share on $1.53 billion in revenue forecast by LSEG. Zscaler's fiscal first-quarter earnings , also released on Monday, likewise surpassed estimates.
